decisions.statement: The command line that starts a seat is composed apart from the spawning of the command line.
A seat's supervisor is reached through the pty proxy rather than run directly.
A seat's supervisor is started by a shell that has read the secrets held outside the repo.
That shell exports every name the secrets file gives.
A secrets file that is not there is no reason to refuse the launch.
The supervisor replaces that shell rather than running beneath it.
The tmux variables of the terminal launching a seat are scrubbed from the inherited environment.
The scrub clears the startup file a bash it hands over to would read.
A tmux server this launch begins is put inside a systemd scope of its own.
That scope bounds how many tasks the tmux server under it may make.
The pane scope tmux makes for a seat bounds how many tasks that seat may make.
No ceiling on processor time is put on the scope a launch makes.
A cap on the scope holds over every process and thread the seat begins.
A seat is bounded by the share the seats hold rather than by a ceiling.
A seat takes the whole machine while nothing else wants it.
The server options are given only on the launch that begins the server.
A seat's agent id reaches its supervisor as an environment value as well as a flag.
A seat begins in the folder above the akasha checkout.
A pane outlives the process that exited in the pane.
An empty prompt is left off the command line rather than given as an empty word.
A launch naming no account is given the default account.
A name a live tmux session already carries refuses the launch.
A pane pid is asked of the pane holding it rather than of the session.
Tmux answers a pane's own values as nothing where a session is named instead.
A session holding no pane is refused.
A session naming no pane pid is refused.
A seat whose session is gone once the seat has had a moment to boot is refused.
A seat's tmux session is named for the seat.
The tmux client is a child of the shell in the tab the client was attached from.
The tmux server is no child of that shell.
The status bar is off.
Nothing here stops a seat or takes the page the seat has.
Nothing here revives a seat whose pane is dead.
A launch onto a tmux server already up makes no scope, so no cap of its own reaches it.
A seat's scratch is put on the disk, because the folder above it is held in memory.

definition: a seat started and put to work
